clue.text: Fellow left with feeling of wanting to scratch side of bacon

parts.note: an itch is the urge to scratch the skin

explanation.surface: A man left with an irritating urge to scratch, in a muddled tale ending with bacon.
explanation.definitionFit: A flitch is an old word for a whole salted and cured side of a pig.

clue.text: Water having awkward rise in blender

parts.note: water is the commonest example of a liquid

indicators.note: awkward suggests the letters of rise are clumsily jumbled into a new order

explanation.surface: Water rising awkwardly inside a kitchen blender as it runs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Water' reads as what goes into the blender, but here it is a general word for any fluid; 'awkward' makes ISER from RISE, and 'having' only joins the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A liquidiser is the British name for a kitchen blender that purees food.

clue.text: Impressions not on board to press down tightly

indicators.note: on board is crossword shorthand for inside SS, a steamship, so these words remove the two S letters

parts.note: stamps are impressions made by pressing a die or seal

explanation.surface: Imprints that never make it onto the board, being pressed firmly instead.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not on board' strips the S and S of a steamship (SS) from STAMPS, its first and last letters, leaving TAMP.
explanation.definitionFit: To tamp is to pack something down firmly, as with tobacco in a pipe or earth in a hole.

clue.text: Similar house for short time has record with lousy centre

parts.note: a mo is a moment, a short time
a log is a written record, as on a ship

indicators.note: centre asks for the middle of the word lousy, without its first and last letters

explanation.surface: A house let briefly comes with a record of having a rotten middle.
explanation.definitionFit: Homologous structures correspond in position or origin, so they are alike in kind.

clue.text: Not one who believes in free speech

definitions.text: Not one who believes in free speech

parts.words: Not one who believes in free speech
parts.note: reads like a censor, but describes someone who interrupts a speaker with jeers, denying the speech a free run

explanation.surface: A description of an opponent of free expression.
explanation.definitionFit: A heckler shouts down speakers, so a speech heckled is anything but freely delivered.

clue.text: Resembling sin?

parts.note: plays on the simile 'as ... as sin', said of something very unattractive

explanation.surface: A question about what looks like wrongdoing.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom 'as ugly as sin' makes sin the standard of hideousness.

clue.text: Necktie card-player may have

explanation.surface: A tie worn by a man dealt cards.
explanation.definitionFit: A four-in-hand is a long tie knotted in a slipknot; a card-player may also hold four cards of a kind in hand.

clue.text: New Delhi, after Sunday, gets protection

indicators.note: after places the new form of Delhi behind the abbreviation for Sunday
New signals a fresh version of the letters of Delhi

explanation.surface: Rebuilt Delhi, after a Sunday, is guarded.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface invites you to read 'New Delhi' as India's capital city, but the first word is the signal: it rearranges DELHI into HIELD, set after the Sunday abbreviation, with 'gets' only linking to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A shield is a piece of armour giving protection, and by extension any safeguard.

clue.text: Above having gradual increase reaching excessive size

parts.note: over means above, as in a lamp over the table
growth is a gradual increase in size

explanation.surface: Something swelling steadily until it gets too large.
explanation.definitionFit: Overgrowth is growth beyond normal bounds, as in a garden run wild.

clue.text: Steeplechaser, one taken aback after spring

indicators.note: after puts the rider behind the word for spring

parts.note: to spring is to jump
read as 'one taken a-back', a rider carried on a horse's back

explanation.surface: A horseman startled after a spring.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taken aback' looks like shock; read it as carried on a back, a horse rider.
explanation.definitionFit: A jump jockey rides in steeplechases and hurdle races over fences rather than on the flat.

clue.text: Romeo has order for gown

parts.note: Romeo is the radio alphabet word for R
the OBE, Order of the British Empire, is a British honour

explanation.surface: Romeo receives an instruction about clothing.
explanation.walkthrough: The OBE is a British honour, the Order of the British Empire.
explanation.definitionFit: A robe is a long loose outer garment, the same kind of dress as a gown.

clue.text: A mother he did not have

definitions.text: A mother he did not have

parts.note: a dam is the mother of an animal, especially a horse

explanation.surface: A man who had no mother.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the definition too: in Genesis the first man was made from dust, not born.
explanation.definitionFit: The first man of Genesis was created directly by God, so he had no parent.

clue.text: Enter claim about commercial

indicators.note: about suggests the letters of enter claim are turned around and reordered

explanation.surface: Lodging a claim about an advertisement.
explanation.definitionFit: Mercantile describes merchants and trade, so it is a synonym of commercial.

clue.text: Was a baby-sitter exposed first without prejudice?

indicators.note: first puts the word for exposed ahead of the word for baby-sitting

parts.note: something exposed is open to view
to mind children is to look after them, so a baby-sitter minded

explanation.surface: A baby-sitter who was caught out first, yet free of bias.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone open-minded receives new ideas fairly, having no preconceived bias.

clue.text: Buffoon almost climbed slope

indicators.note: almost removes the last letter of the word for climbed

parts.note: to mount is to climb, so climbed is mounted
a bank is a sloping piece of ground

explanation.surface: A clown nearly scaled the hillside.
explanation.definitionFit: A mountebank was a quack selling remedies with comic patter; the word extends to a charlatan or clown.

clue.text: Venture to come in with sound award

parts.note: to enter is to come in

indicators.note: sound tells us the word for award is heard, then spelt differently

parts.note: a prize is an award

explanation.surface: Joining a business and winning a good prize.
explanation.walkthrough: PRISE (to lever open) is pronounced exactly like PRIZE.
explanation.definitionFit: An enterprise is a bold undertaking or business project, a venture.

clue.text: Different form of stardom in office of old ruler

indicators.note: a different form of the word stardom is a rearrangement of its letters

explanation.surface: Fame takes another shape in a ruler's office.
explanation.definitionFit: Tsardom is the position or reign of a tsar, the old Russian emperor.

clue.text: Coming from kylesku waiting for middle easterner

indicators.note: Coming from says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Someone waiting in a Scottish village for a visitor from the Middle East.
explanation.walkthrough: Kylesku is a hamlet in the Scottish Highlands. 'for' is a link word, not part of the definition, so the definition is just the last two words.
explanation.definitionFit: A Kuwaiti is a native of Kuwait, a Gulf state in the Middle East.

clue.text: Everyone canned in public debate?

indicators.note: in places the word for everyone inside the container

parts.note: canned food comes in a tin, so canned points to a tin
each means every one, taken individually

explanation.surface: All the participants silenced at a public discussion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'canned' sounds like being sacked or silenced; it points to a tin, with EACH 'in' it.
explanation.definitionFit: A teach-in is an informal public forum, often on a campus, for discussing a political issue.

clue.text: Paper covering double bed?

explanation.surface: A newspaper laid over a large bed.
explanation.definitionFit: A broadsheet is a large-format newspaper; jokingly, a wide sheet is bedding for a double bed.

clue.text: Shameless brother, a Buddhist

parts.note: Zen is a school of Buddhism

explanation.surface: An unashamed sibling who follows Buddhism.
explanation.definitionFit: Brazen means bold and unashamed, as in a brazen lie.

clue.text: It is expected to come out in the wash

definitions.text: It is expected to come out in the wash

parts.words: It is expected to come out in the wash
parts.note: plays on the idiom meaning that a problem will resolve itself, read literally about laundry

explanation.surface: A hopeful remark that things will sort themselves out.
explanation.definitionFit: Grime on clothes is meant to be removed by laundering.

clue.text: Encourage a risk

parts.note: to bet is to risk money on an outcome

explanation.surface: An urging to take a gamble.
explanation.definitionFit: To abet is to encourage or help someone, usually in wrongdoing.

clue.text: Ruby with a vocal exchange using all the words she knows

indicators.note: exchange means the letters swap places to form a new order

explanation.surface: A girl called Ruby trades a vocal line, using every word she knows.
explanation.definitionFit: A person's vocabulary is the stock of words they know and use.

clue.text: Have a look inside for some meat

indicators.note: inside says the answer lies within the words have a look

explanation.surface: An invitation to peer inside in search of meat.
explanation.definitionFit: Veal is the meat of a calf.

clue.text: Unending branch line

parts.note: describes a railway branch that leaves the main line and rejoins it, so it never terminates

explanation.surface: A rail spur that never stops.
explanation.definitionFit: A loop line is a railway track that leaves the main line and rejoins it further on, forming a closed circuit.

clue.text: Larks' transport

definitions.meaning: the collective noun for a group of larks
transport here means rapture or ecstasy, as in transports of delight

explanation.surface: How skylarks get around.
explanation.definitionFit: An exaltation of larks is the traditional group name; exaltation also means intense joy, being transported.

clue.text: Captain did not start fish

indicators.note: did not start removes the first letter of the word for captain

parts.note: a skipper is a ship's captain

explanation.surface: A captain who never set off for his fish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'did not start' drops the S from SKIPPER.
explanation.definitionFit: A kipper is a herring split, salted and smoked.
